correctness.rationale: Each signed coordinate pair independently contributes two, one or zero retained vertices, so (K,L,d-K-L) is multinomial and the hull is a K-crosspolytope with L pyramids when K>=1, otherwise an (L-1)-simplex. The face polynomial follows by multiplying by (1+z) for each pyramid, and intrinsic volumes follow from orthogonal unit-height apexes. Full dimension requires no missing coordinates and K>=1; conditional K is Bin(d,rho) conditioned positive, rho=p/(2-p). Hence R=2^(K-d), Z=2^(d-K)(3^K+1), exact moments by the binomial pgf, full-dimensionality probability and unconditioned ambient-volume moment follow. Binomial LLN/CLT and a bounded log(1+3^(-K)) remainder yield the joint rank-one Gaussian limit; strict logarithmic concavity yields annealed > typical exponent gaps for 0<rho<1. Independently checked the conditional binomial and endpoint d=2,3 canonical face-polynomial identities algebraically; no asymptotic conclusion depends on finite experiments.

value.rationale: Independent vertex thinning of an archetypal centrally symmetric polytope is a natural sparse random-polytope benchmark. Its exact joint combinatorial/geometric spectrum and asymptotic distinction between mean and typical face complexity and volume are useful calibration quantities, not merely an arbitrary face-count table.

limitations: Fixed equal independent retention probability and standard crosspolytope only; not nonuniform retention or general centrally symmetric configurations.
Conditional full-dimensionality becomes rare exponentially; limits do not characterize typical unconditional random hull.
The central multinomial/type observation is elementary and might have appeared in older vertex-percolation polytope literature.
Uniform p and conditioning on a rare full-dimensional event are important for interpreting exponent limits.
